expected.title: Uniform positive-time polynomial velocity tails for rapidly decaying periodic classical non-cutoff Boltzmann solutions with hard potentials and hydrodynamic bounds
expected.author: Cyril Imbert; Clément Mouhot; Luis Silvestre
expected.difficulty_reason: A Carleman hyperplane decomposition separates coercive grazing collisions from three bad terms. Quantitative mass-energy-entropy nonconcentration produces anisotropic cone coercivity, and a singular time-dependent polynomial barrier uses the hard-potential velocity gain to dominate every error independently of initial tail constants.

material.preserved_editorial_scope:
\paragraph{Editorial source boundary.}
Prove only Theorem 1.3(2), reproduced in its original location below, for the stated periodic, nonnegative classical solutions satisfying Definition 1.2 (rapid decay) and the hydrodynamic bounds (1.3), with hard potential \(\gamma\in(0,2)\), \(s\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma+2s\in[0,2]\). The selected conclusion is the full positive-time polynomial velocity upper bound for every \(q>0\), with its original constant dependences. The complete original Sections 2--4 supply the Carleman decomposition, cone coercivity, all error estimates, maximum principle, and singular time-dependent barrier proof. All surrounding author text is necessary/conservative context, and does not create additional selected problems.
